scenario: A summer bike commuter and weekend hiker wants sweet snacks that can ride through a roughly 90-degree afternoon without becoming a leaking, wrapper-stuck mess. Four frozen seller pages show an M&M'S 38-ounce milk-chocolate party bag at 11.79 dollars rated 73 percent over twelve reviews, a 29.99-dollar Skittles tub described as ninety individually wrapped fun-size packets with no posted review, a 7.96-dollar thirteen-ounce Jolly Rancher sour hard-candy bag rated 85 percent over twelve reviews, and a 19.95-dollar six-count Charleston Chew selection described as 1.87-ounce nougat bars with a chocolatey coating and no posted review. The pages describe form, packaging, price and seller wording but do not report a controlled 90-degree pannier or backpack trial, exact melting or glass-transition thresholds, complete current physical labels for every offer, or route-specific safety. General pages define melting point, crystal polymorphism, compound chocolate, hard candy, glass transition, hygroscopy, ice packs and shelf-stable food. Community pages describe one sweat-sogged paper-wrapped candy after a workout, one old large cooler said to stay cold with ice, and a disputed salt-and-ice cooler explanation. None identifies the exact four products under a matched route, bag, exposure, humidity and packaging protocol.
target: Determine what the four frozen seller pages actually establish about price, rating sample, pack, mass, form and packaging, and whether any source proves that an exact snack survives a roughly 90-degree pannier or hiking-pack route. Explain the distinct and limited roles of crystalline melting, polymorphism, compound coating, hard-candy glass transition, humidity uptake, shelf-stable storage and portable cooling without assigning unsupported product thresholds. Keep the three community examples at their exact anecdotal scope. End with a current-label and seal checklist, measurement of the actual bag exposure, a small matched leakproof route trial with cooling treated separately, predeclared mess, texture, waste and burden criteria, and a selection procedure that selects only a passing exact path, uses a proven control, or defers.
